answer: Anchor identity in a collaboration graph: every agent must build working ties with 20 distinct counterparties, each pair co-signing a shared job record. The network measures graph density — genuine agents sit inside a tangled web of ties, while fake farms form star-shaped clusters around one hub. Below the density threshold, an identity stays sandboxed on low-value tasks. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 200,000 distinct counterparty ties, $900,000 in job fees, and 120 days of staged collaboration. Like a terraced garden beside a river, real roots spread wide; a fake is one stem with no soil.
